    BAR H BAR RANCH AND NATURE PRESERVE’S REPLY BRIEF REGARDING
                PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUE NOS. 11 AND 13




                                 1
HB: 4915-1187-6058.1
        I.       INTRODUCTION

             Scimitar Partners LP and Bar H Bar Land & Cattle Co. (collectively, “Bar H Bar Ranch

and Nature Preserve” or “ranch”) files this reply brief regarding preliminary order issue numbers

11 and 13, consistent with State Office of Administrative Hearings (“SOAH”) Order No. 35.

SOAH Order No. 35 required responses on preliminary order issue numbers 11 and 13 to be filed

by October 19, 2026, therefore this pleading is timely filed.

       II.      ARGUMENT

                A. Preliminary Order Issue No. 11

             Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve does not believe that the route proposed in this

proceeding is necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards nor does the evidence in the

docket support such a conclusion. Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA

Transmission Services Corporation (“LCRA”) (collectively, “Joint Applicants”) argue that

“ERCOT' s study of the Permian Basin under those standards revealed that the existing system

does not meet them identifying thermal overloads, voltage instability, and future conditions the

system simply cannot support. This is a reliability standard violation that requires a solution. The

PBRP, and the Import Path 2 Projects within it, were the solution recommended to correct those

NERC reliability violations.” 1 However, under PURA § 37.056(a), Joint Applicants bear the

burden of affirmatively proving that this project clears the reliability threshold; the Permian Basin

Reliability Plan’s (“PRBP”) prior approval does not substitute for that proof. The Join Applicants

provided no evidence outside of the PRBP to support that the transmission line was needed to meet

state or federal reliability standards. Further, the SOAH Proposal for Decision (“PFD”) already



1
    Applicant’s Brief on Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13 at 4 (Oct. 7, 2026).

                                                            2
HB: 4915-1187-6058.1
 discussed this issue in depth stating that “[a] 765-kV transmission line authorized to transmit bulk

power into the Permian Basin cannot be shown to be needed for reliability when the record

establishes that the analysis of whether the grid can actually deliver that reliability has not been

done. Accordingly, the ALJs conclude Applicants have failed to show that Import Path 2-a $4-to-

$5-billion infrastructure commitment-is necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience,

or safety of the public. The ALJs, therefore, recommend in their conclusion on need that the

Commission deny the CCN Applications for both Projects.” 2 Further, the PFD states that Joint

Applicant’s own witness admitted that Joint Applicants “had not performed a partial build study

to justify Import Path 2 individually. 3 Next, the PFD correctly points out that there was no

independent analysis of Import Path 2 to justify its need to comply with NERC Reliability

standards. 4 The PFD therefore concluded that though NERC contingencies can and should

influence ERCOT’s regional planning, they are not a subsisted in a transmission line Certificate

of Convenience and Necessity (“CCN”) proceeding for the Joint Applicants proving the project-

specific need for Import Path 2. 5 The PFD already covered this issue and got it right the first time,

Joint Applicants did not independently prove need for the project to meet state or federal reliability

standards and failed to meet their burden of proof for approval of the project.

            The PFD put it better that Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve could the first time, simply

put the Joint Applicants’ “failed to show the PBRP's underlying projected loads establish a need

for Import Path 2. Instead, the record proves that the projected loads ̶ because of changed

circumstances ̶ do not support these proposed transmission Projects but instead should be re-


2
    Proposal for Decision at 87 (Aug. 20, 2026).
3
    Id. at 88.
4

5
    Id. at 89.


                                                     3
HB: 4915-1187-6058.1
 evaluated.” 6 The Joint Applicants have failed to show a reliability need for the project that meets

the burden required by PURA and therefore the PFD got it right the first time by recommending

denial of the application. 7

                 B. Preliminary Order Issue No. 13

            Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve does not believe that the project proposed in this

proceeding will provide congestion cost savings for consumers that justifies the cost of the project

nor does the evidence in the docket support such a conclusion. The Joint Applicants point out that

because this is a reliability project they do not need to prove congestion cost savings for consumers.

Joint Applicants then point to only anecdotal evidence of cost savings by arguing that the project

would save money as compared to a 345-kV alternative and that the West Texas transmission

system accounts for $3 billion in cost to consumers from 2020 to 2024. 8 However, the Joint

Applicants provided no proof that the project independently would save consumers money. Nor

did they differentiate how Import Path 2 would save consumers money compared to the other

Import Paths being proposed or alternatives to constructing Import Path 2 or any of the other

Import Paths. Joint Applicants did not meet their burden of proof because they provided no

independent evidence or analysis that Import Path 2 on its own would congestion cost savings for

consumers.

            Again, the PFD gets it right the first time on this issue regarding congestion cost savings

to consumers. First, the PFD states “[t]he Project is a reliability project. Only economic projects

require an analysis of the estimated cost to consumers and any consumer congestion cost savings.



6
    Id. at 99.
7
    Applicant’s Brief on Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13 at 16 (Oct. 7, 2026).
8
    Id.


                                                            4
HB: 4915-1187-6058.1
 As a reliability project, the estimated cost of the facilities to consumers, and congestion-cost-

savings analysis are not required under Rule 25.101(b)(3)(A)(i) and (b)(3)(A)(ii).” 9 Next, the PFD

states that “Applicants did not submit the estimated cost of the facilities to consumers or the

estimated congestion cost savings to consumers that may result from the proposed transmission

facilities.” 10 Lastly, the PFD states “[t]he analysis for the cost to consumers and congestion cost

savings is not required, and the record contains no evidence quantifying either.” 11 The PFD already

covered this issue and concluded there is no record evidence to support that the proposed project

would lead to congestion cost savings to consumers. Therefore, this issue does not support

reversing the original PFD recommendation given there is no record evidence to support savings

to consumers. Therefore, the PFD should continue to recommend denial of the application in this

proceeding.

       III.      CONCLUSION

              Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve strongly opposes selection of route 894 or any other

alternative route that utilizes links H1 or G52. Further, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve

believes that the PFD did adequately cover Preliminary Order Issue numbers 11 and 13 in the

original PFD. In the PFD, the SOAH ALJs found that the project was not needed for reliability

reasons and that there was no record evidence supporting that the project would provide congestion

cost savings to consumers. The PFD got it right the first time, there is no need for the project

proposed by the Joint Applicants and the application should be denied in line with the PFD’s

original recommendation.
